title: Lace a board's next eyelet, handing the lace's tip through the hole from one hand to the other
instruction: Push the lace's blue tip through the second eyelet with one hand and keep hold of it until the other hand has taken the tip behind the board; then let go, and with the other hand pull the lace on through until the whole tip is through.
context: Lacing shoes is an everyday skill, practised on lacing boards in occupational therapy and by children, and helping someone with their laces is a common caring task. Each eyelet takes a handover: the tip is pushed through by one hand and taken on the far side by the other.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed upright beech-plywood lacing board along the forward direction on the centre line, from 20 to 40 cm forward, 14 cm tall and 4 mm thick, on a foot; its front faces left (toward the left arm). Two nickel-plated brass eyelets go through it 12 cm above the table, 26 and 34 cm forward, 22 mm across inside; the second has a brass funnel 3.6 cm across on its front. (2) A white braided polyester lace about 29 cm long and 6 mm thick, knotted behind the first eyelet (the knot 2.8 cm across). It comes out of the first eyelet to the left, hangs in a loop and ends in a stiff blue plastic (acetate) tip 9 cm long and 1 cm thick. (3) The tip rests on two fixed wooden pegs, 34 cm forward and 12 cm above the table, pointing right at the second eyelet, from 4.5 to 13.5 cm left of the board. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. Through: the lace crosses the board's plane inside the second eyelet. Handed over: from the moment the tip is 1 cm out behind the board until the whole tip is through, some gripper's fingertip centre (TCP) stays within 3 cm of the tip; letting go of it in the eyelet loses the handover. 1.0: through, the tip's back end at least 1.2 cm out behind the board, and handed over; 0.5: the tip 1 cm out behind the board through the second eyelet; 0.25: the tip into the second eyelet at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with the lace still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Pull the lace back out of the second eyelet, leave it knotted through the first, and rest its tip on the two pegs pointing at the second eyelet.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the lace is a chain of 15 short rigid pieces on ball joints (it bends only at the joints and does not stretch), and its tip a rigid rod; the board and its eyelets are rigid and slick. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
